zones.label: Check the Scene
zones.summary: Pause long enough to notice hazards before approaching.
facts: Protect yourself from traffic, fire, electricity, chemicals, or violence.
Get an adult and keep others back when the scene is unsafe.

zones.label: Recognize
zones.summary: Look for unresponsiveness, breathing trouble, severe bleeding, choking, or other urgent signs.
facts: Do not delay help while trying to name the exact condition.
Use calm observation and share what you see.

zones.label: Call for Help
zones.summary: Activate a trusted adult and emergency services quickly.
facts: Give the location and describe what is happening.
Follow dispatcher instructions and send someone to guide responders.

zones.label: Choking Response
zones.summary: Severe choking requires immediate trained action and emergency activation.
facts: Age and condition affect the correct response.
Practice only with qualified instruction; never rehearse forcefully on a person.

zones.label: Emergency Medication
zones.summary: Emergency medication should follow the person’s plan and trained adult guidance.
facts: Examples may include epinephrine or rescue inhalers.
Call emergency services when the plan or symptoms require it.
